title: Wearable-data models evaluate near-term binge-eating risk
summary: In a four-week observational study of 30 adults with recurrent binge eating, random-forest models used smartwatch physiology or self-reported affect to evaluate episode risk. The first three weeks trained models and the final week tested them within the same participants. Sensor-only AUROC was 0.78, with sensitivity 0.92 but specificity 0.35; macro-averaged accuracy did not significantly exceed self-report. No model met both prespecified sensitivity and specificity thresholds, and benefits from adaptive intervention remain untested.

source_review.scope: Primary full article Methods, Results and limitations plus Europe PMC bibliographic metadata; PMC full article.

evidence.tested: Within-participant temporal hold-out comparison of sensor, self-report and combined models.
evidence.unknown: New-participant performance, deployable specificity and benefits of model-triggered therapy remain unestablished.
evidence.ai_role: Elastic-net selects sensor features on training data; RF combines person/group models with tuning inside first-three-week data and tests on last week. Chronological retrospective evaluation is not prospective model-guided intervention. Source discussion has a sensitivity/specificity wording error; numerical Results and tables support 0.92 sensitivity and 0.35 specificity.
